name: file-token-group
purpose: Use FileTokenGroup for the files picked in a form field, before and during upload; a transfer that runs in the background while the person keeps working is an UploadProgress. The files a person picked for upload, shown as removable tokens before or while they upload: each token names the file with a glyph for its type, its size and, when asked, its last-modified date, carries a progress bar while it uploads and its own error or warning line when it cannot be sent. It pairs with `file-dropzone` (which receives the files) and with a Browse files button: the product keeps the list, the group renders it and reports which token was removed. Taken from Cloudscape's file token group; the Console Kit and the design sample list files by hand.
useWhen: Under a `FileDropzone` or a Browse files button in a form, to show what will be uploaded and let the person drop a file before submitting.
In an upload dialog, to show each file's progress and the files that were refused (too large, wrong type) with the reason.
Read-only, in a review step, to list the attachments that will be sent.
avoidWhen: A running transfer that should follow the person around the console → use `upload-progress`.
Files already stored in a bucket or a repository → use `table` (the file browser block).
Free-text tags or labels → use `tag-editor` or `chip`.
related: `file-dropzone` — receives dropped files; the group lists them.

`upload-progress` — the floating card for transfers that keep running after the dialog closes. Split: FileTokenGroup lists the files picked in a form, before and while they are sent, and dies with the form; UploadProgress tracks transfers that outlive the dialog, with Cancel and Retry. Both draw a file row with a progress bar; when a transfer must survive navigation, hand it to UploadProgress instead of keeping the token.
`chip` — a removable label without file details.
bestPractices: Keep the refused files in the list with their error, so the person sees why and can remove them; do not drop them silently.
Write each error as the reason and the limit (`Larger than 300 MB`), not as a code.
Use `limit` when more than five files are common, so the form below stays in view.
Remove the file from your list on `remove`; the group moves focus to the next token for you.

props.name: items
props.doc: The files, in order; each with its optional upload state, error and warning.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Vertical stacks full-width tokens; horizontal wraps compact tokens in rows. Same name as `field`'s axis.

props.name: limit
props.doc: Shows this many tokens and a Show more toggle for the rest. 0 shows them all.

props.name: showFileSize
props.doc: Shows the size beside the name, formatted for the locale.

props.name: showFileLastModified
props.doc: Shows the last-modified date, formatted for the locale.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Hides the remove buttons; the list is for reading only.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Files`).

events.name: remove
events.payload: (event: MouseEvent, payload: { index: number; item: FileTokenGroupItem })
events.notes: The remove button of the token at `index` was pressed. The parent removes it from `items`. Same name as Chip and AttributeEditor.
